questions.prompt: Which are signs that a chemical reaction may have happened? Choose all that apply.
options: A solid forms when two solutions mix
The substance is moved to a new container
questions.explain: Gas, colour change, temperature change, precipitate (plus light or sound) are signs of a reaction.

questions.prompt: Carbon dioxide gas is bubbled through lime water. What do you observe?
questions.explain: Lime water turns milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms. This is the test for carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Match each reaction to its main sign.
questions.explain: Each reaction shows a different sign of a new substance forming.

questions.prompt: Sort into exothermic (gives out heat) and endothermic (takes in heat).
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions release energy; endothermic reactions absorb it.

questions.prompt: An iron nail is left in blue copper sulfate solution. After some time, what do you observe?
options: The solution turns pale green and a brown coating forms on the nail
questions.explain: Iron displaces copper: green iron sulfate forms in the solution and brown copper coats the nail.

questions.prompt: You open a bottle of soda and it fizzes. Is this a chemical reaction?
options: Yes, bubbles always mean a reaction
Yes, because it makes a sound
No: dissolved carbon dioxide is just escaping, and no new substance forms
No, because soda is a liquid

feedback.0: Bubbles are only a clue. Here, no new substance is made.

questions.explain: The gas was already dissolved under pressure. Opening the bottle lets it escape: a physical change.

questions.text: A solid that forms when two solutions are mixed is called a ___. A reaction that gives out heat is ___.
questions.explain: Precipitate = solid formed from solutions. Exothermic = gives out heat.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to test the gas from baking soda and vinegar.
steps: Put baking soda in a test tube and add vinegar
Quickly fit a stopper with a delivery tube
Dip the end of the tube into lime water
Observe whether the lime water turns milky
Conclude whether the gas is carbon dioxide
questions.explain: React → collect the gas → test it → observe → conclude.

questions.prompt: Two clear solutions are mixed. The temperature rises from 25 °C to 31 °C and the mixture turns cloudy. What is the best conclusion?
options: A chemical reaction happened: it is exothermic and a precipitate formed
questions.explain: Two signs together (temperature rise and a solid forming) are strong evidence of an exothermic reaction making a precipitate.

questions.prompt: Describe how you could show that the gas produced when chalk reacts with vinegar is carbon dioxide.
questions.modelAnswer: Put chalk pieces in a test tube and add vinegar. Fit a stopper with a delivery tube and bubble the gas through lime water in another tube. If the lime water turns milky, the gas is carbon dioxide.
rubric: I described reacting chalk with vinegar
I passed the gas into lime water
I said lime water turning milky shows carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Always name the test (lime water) and the result (turns milky).
